title: Making the invisible visible: Use of whole-body photography for early detection and telemonitoring of vitiligo in southern Germany
summary:
The primary objective of this project is to evaluate the approach of offering telemedical full-body photography for individuals affected by vitiligo, while simultaneously guiding them through the digital patient journey to raise awareness of the disease, as well as diagnostic and therapeutic options. VitiligoVision adopts the concept of the official health portal of the German Federal Ministry of Health, Gesund.bund.de, which provides scientifically sound, comprehensible, and trustworthy health information to the general public, and applies this principle specifically to the care of individuals with vitiligo.

Through an accessible digital platform, medical content is presented in a transparent and low-threshold manner, with the goal of strengthening health literacy and actively involving patients in their healthcare decisions. The project combines digital information dissemination with evidence-based recommendations to enable patients to make informed choices regarding their healthcare.

Whereas Gesund.bund.de assists the public in making informed health decisions, VitiligoVision bridges the gap between the search for information and concrete healthcare provision. It achieves this by linking digital educational materials with specific care pathways for individuals with vitiligo.¹⁷

Moreover, the project seeks to identify the needs and unmet expectations of those affected by vitiligo, as well as to analyse the barriers and challenges that patients encounter in accessing guideline-based, modern treatments for the condition. In parallel, the project will assess the acceptance of telemedical 2D full-body photography among patients.

This innovative project, which extends beyond the boundaries of conventional medical care, ultimately contributes to a deeper understanding of the treatment landscape for vitiligo and facilitates optimised access to dermatological care for those affected.

interventions.name:
All patients receive teledermatology treatment.
A subgroup will also undergo a qualitative interview
. Patients diagnosed with vitiligo
are monitored with whole-body photography.
